subject: Culture
title: The Good Death
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Good Death usable.

hook.text: Medieval Christians spent lives preparing to die well. A 'good death' meant confessing, forgiving, and being awake.

buildup.text: The 'Ars Moriendi'—Art of Dying—was one of the most popular books of the 1400s, outselling everything but the Bible.

discovery.text: Hindu tradition considers dying in Varanasi and being cremated on the Ganges the ideal death—instant liberation.

twist.text: Modern medicine turned death into a failure. We moved it from home to hospitals, hiding what was once communal.

climax.text: The hospice movement reverses this—returning dignity, choice, and ritual to the dying process.

punchline.text: How you die says as much about your culture as how you live.
